instruction: Rotate the dog image 90 degrees clockwise in GIMP.

command: import time; import pyautogui; time.sleep(1); pyautogui.hotkey(['shift', 'ctrl', 'e']);
import time; import pyautogui; time.sleep(1); pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 'a'); time.sleep(0.3); pyautogui.write('dog_rotated'); time.sleep(1); pyautogui.press('enter');
import time; import pyautogui; time.sleep(1); pyautogui.press('enter');

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened GIMP with the dog image, dismissed color profile dialog, added alpha channel via Layer > Transparency, attempted background removal using Select by Color, Fuzzy Select, and Free Select tools for 50 turns but failed to complete the task.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate GIMP menus (File, Edit, Select, Image, Layer, Colors, Tools, View), add alpha channel, use selection tools, zoom in/out, handle dialogs
metadata.failure_analysis: Model failed at the complex multi-step background removal workflow. It could navigate menus and use tools individually but couldn't complete the precise background selection + deletion + export pipeline within 50 turns.
metadata.task_rationale: Decomposed original task into a single-step image transformation (rotate 90° CW) via Image > Transform menu. The model demonstrated it can navigate Image menu, so this should be achievable. Original image is 1578x948, so after 90° CW rotation it becomes 948x1578.
metadata.explanation: Task requires rotating the image 90° clockwise using Image > Transform > Rotate 90° clockwise. Postconfig exports as dog_rotated.png. Custom getter reads exported file dimensions with PIL. Metric checks that width=948 and height=1578 (swapped from original 1578x948) with partial credit.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the exported image file from VM and extracts width/height using PIL.
Metric correctly accesses expected parameter directly (expected.get('expected_width')) — proper handling for type='rule'.
Expected values are correct: original 1578x948 becomes 948x1578 after 90° rotation.
Postconfig correctly exports the image via Shift+Ctrl+E, renames to dog_rotated, and confirms export.
Partial credit scoring (0.5 per dimension) is reasonable for this task.
Minor limitation: dimension check cannot distinguish between CW and CCW rotation, as both produce identical width/height swaps. A pixel-level comparison would be needed to verify rotation direction.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: To fully verify 90° CW (vs CCW), consider adding a pixel-level check (e.g., compare a corner pixel of the rotated image against expected value from the original image's corresponding position after CW rotation).
